_note: Every background run gets a WALL-CLOCK BUDGET, and the run RECORD is what an author actually reads (parity/F08-background.md). Three pure facts, shared by all three renderers: the countdown an action reads as dsx.module.background.context.remaining while it runs; the run-record fold that turns a sequence of lifecycle facts into one honest lastResult, including the case nobody handles (the OS killed the process mid-flight, which must still be recorded on the next launch rather than leaving a run that looks like it is forever running); and the release gate on `run`, which exists so nobody can fake a scheduler in production and ship an app whose background work has never once been exercised by the OS.
_note_budgets: iOS gives a background task roughly 30 seconds before the expiration handler fires; Android WorkManager gives a worker roughly 10 minutes before it is stopped. Both are the platform's numbers, not ours, and neither is a guarantee: the OS may expire a run sooner. Exceeding the budget is the typed budget_exceeded outcome, recorded as a failed run, never a silent kill.
